title: Internal Audit
outcomes: Explain internal audit and section 138 applicability.
Maintain independence and perform internal audit engagements.
Report findings and relate internal and external audit.

meta.exam_tip: Check rule 13 thresholds carefully — public and private companies differ.

concepts.title: Internal audit: meaning, applicability and scope
body: Internal audit independently assures the board and management that controls and risk management are working, strengthening governance and helping the organisation achieve its objectives. ICAI's Internal Audit Standards Board issues Standards on Internal Audit (SIAs) and guidance.

Section 138 with rule 13 requires internal auditors for listed companies, and unlisted public companies or private companies meeting thresholds (e.g. paid-up capital ₹50 crore or more for public companies, turnover ₹200 crore or more, borrowings over ₹100 crore, or deposits of ₹25 crore or more for public companies). The internal auditor may be a CA, cost accountant or other professional decided by the board, and may be an employee.
Scope covers operational, financial, compliance and IT areas, risk management and governance, as decided by the board or audit committee.
concepts.analogy: Internal audit protects the organisation from the inside.
concepts.work: A private company crossing ₹200 crore turnover must appoint an internal auditor.

concepts.title: Independence, qualities and performing the engagement
body: Integrity, objectivity and independence are essential: the internal auditor should have functional reporting to the audit committee, avoid conflicts, and not perform operational duties they later audit.
Qualities: professional competence, skepticism, communication skills, understanding of business and technology, and ethical conduct.
Performing the engagement: plan based on risk, understand processes, gather and analyse evidence, document work, review and communicate findings, and follow up on implementation.
concepts.analogy: Independence of mind and of reporting lines makes internal audit credible.
concepts.work: An internal auditor reporting directly to the audit committee is more independent.

concepts.title: Internal audit reports and the relationship with external audit
body: Internal audit reports present observations, root causes, risk ratings, recommendations and management responses, communicated to management and the audit committee; assurance reports state the scope, criteria and conclusion.

The external auditor may use internal audit work (SA 610) after evaluating the function's objectivity, competence and systematic approach, and may use internal auditors for direct assistance where not prohibited, under supervision, excluding significant judgements.
Internal audit is a management function supporting governance; it does not replace management's responsibility for controls.
concepts.analogy: Internal and external auditors cooperate but stay distinct.
concepts.work: Internal audit reports feed the audit committee's oversight.

concepts.title: Audit trail under the Companies Act
body: An audit trail (edit log) is a chronological record of changes to accounting data — who changed what, when, and old and new values — enabling tracing from reports back to source.

Companies using accounting software must use software with an audit trail feature that records every transaction and edit, cannot be disabled, and is preserved for the statutory period (Companies (Accounts) Rules, proviso to rule 3(1)); auditors report on this under Rule 11(g).
Internal auditors review audit trail configuration, access to change it, and exceptions such as back-dated or deleted entries.
concepts.analogy: Every edit must leave a footprint that cannot be switched off.
concepts.work: An ERP setting that disables edit logs for some users breaches the rules.

illustrations.title: Is internal audit mandatory?
illustrations.q: Jade Pvt Ltd. has paid-up capital of ₹40 lakh and no loans; its turnover in the last three years was ₹49 crore, ₹145 crore and ₹260 crore (most recent). Must it appoint an internal auditor under section 138 and rule 13?

head: Test (private company)
Threshold
Jade
rows: Over ₹100 crore at any time in preceding year

checks.label: Turnover in the preceding year (₹ crore)

illustrations.title: Using internal audit work
illustrations.q: The statutory auditor wants to use the internal audit team's work on fixed asset verification. The internal audit head reports to the CFO, whose bonus depends on profit. What should be evaluated?

head: Factor
Evaluation
rows: Reporting to CFO with profit-linked bonus may impair objectivity; check access to audit committee
Lower where judgement or risk is high; perform own procedures
solution.title: SA 610 evaluation

jobs.title: Setting up internal audit
jobs.situation: A company has just crossed section 138 thresholds.
steps: Get board approval for scope and charter.
Execute audits and report to the audit committee.
jobs.takeaway: A charter and risk-based plan make internal audit effective.

viva.model: An independent check that controls and risk processes work well, which strengthens governance and supports objectives.

viva.q: Which companies need internal auditors under section 138?
viva.model: Listed companies and unlisted public or private companies crossing thresholds of capital, turnover, borrowings or deposits.

viva.q: How is internal audit independence protected?
viva.model: Through reporting to the audit committee, avoiding operational roles and conflicts, and unrestricted access.
A chronological record of changes to accounting data showing who changed what and when, with old and new values.

viva.q: What does an internal audit report contain?
viva.model: Observations, root causes, risk ratings, recommendations and management responses.

cases.title: First Fintech Ltd.
cases.case: First Fintech, a listed company, uses accounting software where the audit trail was switched off for two months during a migration. Its internal audit head also approves vendor payments. The statutory auditor wants to rely on internal audit's testing of payables.

mcqs.q: Switching off the audit trail breaches:
options: The Companies (Accounts) Rules on audit trail
mcqs.explain: Must not be disabled. In practice: report under Rule 11(g).
